cohort: The study participants were 50,043 and 62,984 low-risk birthing individuals from two national community birth registries.
finding: Planned home births are as safe as planned birth center births for low-risk pregnancies, with outcomes being largely comparable or suggesting home birth was safer for some neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Individuals who planned home births had a lower incidence of all types of transfers compared to those who planned birth center births, but in one dataset, they experienced more cesareans.
